definition: This element specifies the body of a WordprocessingML document, which contains the main document story. It houses the primary block-level content, such as paragraphs, tables, and the section properties for the final section of the document.

Specifies that the contents of the current table row must not be split across multiple pages when a page break occurs. If the row cannot fit on the remainder of the page, the entire row is moved to the start of the next page.
Specifies the root element for the main document part of a WordprocessingML document. It contains the body element, which holds the primary document content such as paragraphs, tables, and sections.

Specifies a paragraph of content within a WordprocessingML document. It is the basic unit of block-level content, containing optional paragraph properties and one or more inline runs of text, drawings, or fields.
Specifies a run of content in a WordprocessingML document. It acts as a container for inline elements and text that share a common set of properties, such as formatting and styles.
Specifies the literal text content of a run in a WordprocessingML document. This element contains the actual string data to be displayed and can preserve whitespace through the xml:space attribute.

Specifies a table in a WordprocessingML document. A table is a block-level element that contains a set of table rows and cells, which are used to arrange text, images, and other content in a grid structure.

Specifies that the current table row shall be repeated at the top of each new page on which the table is displayed, acting as a header row. This is used for multi-page tables to ensure the header row remains visible.

Defines a single cell within a table row of a table. It acts as a container for block-level elements, such as paragraphs and nested tables, which hold the actual cell content. It also contains cell-specific properties that define formatting and layout rules for the cell.
Specifies a single row within a table in a WordprocessingML document. This element acts as a container for table cells (tc) and row-level formatting properties (trPr).
Specifies the root element for a PresentationML document, containing presentation-wide properties such as slide size, notes size, default text styles, and references to slide masters and slides.
Slide. The root element representing a single slide within the presentation.

This element specifies an instance of a slide layout. It contains a template slide design that can be applied to any slide in a presentation, defining the default positioning and formatting of placeholders and other shapes.

Specifies an instance of a slide master slide. It contains all elements that describe the objects and their corresponding formatting for slides within a presentation, including shapes, text styles, color maps, and transitions.

This element specifies the existence of a single shape. A shape can either be a preset or a custom geometry defined using the DrawingML framework, and can have visual properties, non-visual properties, text, and styling attached.

This element specifies the text body to be contained within a shape in a presentation. It houses all the visible text, paragraph formatting, and text body properties such as columns and wrapping. The text within this element is structured into one or more paragraphs containing text runs.
Specifies a default content type that will be associated with all parts in the package that have the extension specified in the Extension attribute.
Content Type Override. Specifies the content type of a specific part inside the ZIP package, overriding defaults.
Defines a single relationship between a source package or part and a target resource. It specifies a unique identifier, the relationship type (defining its role), and the target URI.

The Relationships element is the root element of a relationship part (.rels) in an Open Packaging Conventions (OPC) package. It acts as a container for one or more Relationship elements that define associations between a source part and target resources.

The Types element is the root element of the Content Types stream ([Content_Types].xml) in an OPC package. It contains the default and override content type mappings that define the media types for all parts in the package.
Represents a cell in a worksheet. It is the core container for cell data, including its value, formula, style formatting index, and data type.

Defines the formula expression for a cell, which can be a normal, shared, array, or data table formula. It contains the formula string as its text content and supports various attributes to control calculation behavior, cell ranges, and sharing.

This element represents a single row in a worksheet's grid and acts as a container for the individual cells (c) within that row. It defines row-level properties including the 1-based row index (r), custom height (ht), style formatting index (s), outline level, and visibility states such as hidden or collapsed.

The sheetData element represents the table grid of a worksheet in a SpreadsheetML document. It acts as the container for all row and cell elements, organizing the actual cell data and formulas of the sheet.
This element represents an individual string in the Shared String Table. It can contain either a simple text value or a complex set of rich text runs with character-level formatting.

The sst element defines the Shared String Table, which stores a single unique copy of each text string used across all worksheets in the spreadsheet. Rather than repeating literal strings in individual cells, cells reference these strings by their zero-based index to optimize file size. It also records the total and unique count of strings in the workbook.

The Cell Value element expresses the direct value of a worksheet cell. It contains the raw data, such as a numeric value, a boolean representation, an error code, or a zero-based index pointing to a shared string in the shared string table.

Represents the root element of a worksheet in a SpreadsheetML document. It contains all the sheets' data, columns, rows, cell formatting, and other properties that define the structure and content of an individual sheet.
